hook_text: Let go of a blown-up balloon and it zooms across the room. A giant space rocket works the same way!
clip_script: Pretoria. A classroom full of strings. Three, two, one: let go! Air whooshes out the back, and the balloon zooms forward. That is a rocket! Push gas backwards, get pushed forwards. A real rocket burns fuel in its engine. Hot gas blasts out of the nozzle, and up it goes. Nose cone at the top, fuel tanks in the middle, fins at the bottom. Input: fuel. Process: burning. Output: lift off!
visual_style: Whiteboard balloon taped to a straw on a string, air rushing out of the back and the balloon zooming forward, then a tall rocket with labels for the nose cone, fuel tanks, engine, nozzle and fins, with hot gas shooting down and the rocket moving up.
mood: Lively and hands-on, like a science experiment that makes everyone cheer.
pacing: The balloon rocket experiment first, then the push-back idea, then the parts of a real rocket as a system with input, process and output.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build your own balloon rocket on a string.
